description: A pure CALCULATION node — keep only the detections whose label matches. Splits ONE Object Detection result into families (doors / windows / rooms) so a single API call replaces one call per class. Draws nothing on canvas.
instructions:
A value-only node: it takes a labelled detection and returns the subset whose label matches, on the SAME endpoint names Object Detection publishes — so it drops straight into wiring that already expects a detection.

WHY IT EXISTS: asking Gemini for "door, window, room" in ONE call costs a fraction of three separate calls, but every box then arrives on one pair of endpoints. Wire that one detection into three of these — match "door", "window", "room" — and you get the three families back, each ready for Label Graph and Merge Graph.

INPUT: wire Object Detection's val-polygons into valin-polygons AND its val-labels into valin-labels. Filtering is by INDEX — label i belongs to ring i — so BOTH must come from the same detection node, and the labels endpoint is not optional. You may wire val-graph into valin-graph instead of polygons; components are then filtered by the same index rule. Polygons win when both are supplied, because a ring list carries the boundary vertices exactly.

MATCH is a comma-separated list of terms: "door" keeps every label containing "door" (so "door", "Door", "sliding door" and "doorway" all match), and "door, gate" keeps either. Matching is case-insensitive and matches in BOTH directions, so the term "door" also keeps a label of "dr" only if one contains the other — set Match mode to "Exact" when you need the label to equal the term. Invert keeps everything that does NOT match, which is how you collect the leftovers into a "furniture" catch-all after the named families have been taken. An EMPTY match passes everything through unchanged (inverted: nothing), so an unconfigured node is visibly inert rather than silently emptying the branch.

OUTPUT: val-polygons (the kept rings as a nested [[[x,y],…],…] metre list), val-graph (the kept rings as node/edge JSON, one closed component per ring, each edge already carrying its `label`), val-labels (the kept names, same order), val-count and val-area (m²). Chain val-graph + val-labels into Label Graph to stamp the family's type and thickness, then Merge Graph.

Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
